shared_elements: broad rectangular block/head atop a narrower shaft (T-like silhouette)
low-relief carving on the shaft surface
animal or creature figure in relief on the shaft
vertical elongated raised element running down the shaft (arm/limb-like)
justification: Both are large upright stone monoliths in which a broad rectangular top block sits on a narrower body, with relief carving confined to the shaft and a small animal figure set against a long vertical limb-like ridge — a genuinely comparable anthropomorphic pillar scheme. The rendering differs sharply, however: A is densely covered in fine, crisp curvilinear motifs including a prominent chest disc and banded skirt, while B carries only sparse, shallow, weathered relief on an otherwise plain surface, and the two differ in stone colour and context (museum display versus in-situ excavation).
